name: Belgium: Part II package and CTIS upload check
applies_to: each Belgium package (fr, nl, de) and the shared Belgian administrative documents, as a whole (plan-level checklist step)

items.check: BE-K1 recruitment and informed consent procedure on the EU template, with a section for every pathway in the plan, uploaded under K.59 and L.62.
BE-K2 recruitment material present for every advertisement or recruitment item used.
BE-L1 main ICF per adult population on the current CT-College template, in every required regional language, with the sponsor statement if required.
Every population that cannot use the standard adult-patient form has its own BE-L1-POPULATION set (population_sets).
BE-L2 other patient-facing documents needing ethics review present; endpoint instruments placed in Part I.
For every principal investigator at each Belgian site: BE-M1 CV (with GCP evidence) and BE-M2 declaration of interest.
BE-N1 site suitability statement for every site, signed by the head of the institution or a delegate.
BE-O1 insurance certificate with the insured amount and reference to national legislation.
BE-P-FINANCING Belgian Statement on financing (national form) under P.69.
BE-P1 participant compensation on the EU template.
BE-P3 site financial arrangements and agreements (draft contract or financing statement) for each site.
BE-R1 GDPR statement present because the ICF lacks the GDPR confirmation.
BE-S1 biological-sample form with Belgian section 5.1 text and scope declaration.
No separate planned-site list and no proof of fee payment uploaded; patient cards and purely operational instructions not uploaded unless they could affect the decision to participate.

Every Belgian site has the correct regional participant-language set (nl Flanders, fr Wallonia, de German-speaking region, fr and nl in Brussels as the population requires), and every language version is submitted.
Every language version of a participant document matches the others document for document and version for version, with CT-College standard text in each official language.
German documents: the implementation of the mandatory template agreed with FAMHP or the CT-College and the translation approach documented.
items.applies_when: participants recruited in the German-speaking region

items.check: Administrative documents are in Dutch, French, German or English.
Blank ICFs are unsigned; site suitability statements are signed by the correct institutional signatory; no other document signed merely for submission.
Participant numbers, payments, procedures and sample plans match across CTIS, the protocol, site statements and ICFs.
Compensation amounts and conditions identical in P1, the financing statement, the site agreements and every participant document.
Insurance wording in every participant document matches the O1 certificate.
Sample types, storage, scope (same disease, treatment or drug, or biobank) and anonymisation choices identical in S1, the protocol and the participant documents.
Consent pathways in K1 match the L1 sets in the package.
Title, EU trial number, treatment arms, visits, sample volumes, risks and contraception match the protocol in every ICF.
Documents adapted from the reference package contain all Belgian national content and no leftovers from the reference country or language.
items.applies_when: Belgium or this language is not the reference package

items.check: Correct B–S section prefix and CTIS placeholder for each document (K.59, K.60, L.61 to L.63, M.65, M.66, N, O, P.69 to P.71, R, S).

Unique, self-explanatory title of at most 100 characters: <section code>_<document type>_<subtype>_<country>_<language>_<special attribute>, with only the fields that distinguish the document; _BE_fr, _BE_nl or _BE_de where the language distinguishes it.
Version numbers and dates entered in CTIS structured data, not in the title or filename.
Annex I letter and document language in the filename where practical (FAMHP); filename base contains none of ( ) / , . ; | [ ] (the period before the extension is fine).
Personal names only where disclosure permits (principal investigator in M1/M2).
Clean, tracked-change, redacted or public and split-file variants clearly distinguished; tracked-change versions provided with RFI responses and substantial modifications.
Article 11 workaround: every mandatory Part II placeholder holds the official placeholder PDF titled Part_II_placeholder_document_Article_11_workaround.
items.applies_when: Belgium receives Part I only under Article 11

items.check: For each document, publication status checked against the current Annex I publication tables.
Signatures, personal addresses and other unnecessary personal data removed from documents intended for CTIS publication.
CCI redaction only after both tests: not in the public domain, and disclosure would undermine a legitimate economic interest.
Public and assessment versions differ only by the intended redactions; each in the correct CTIS slot.
No personal data or CCI in public structured fields.
No drafting instruction remains in any document (see content/conventions/template-instructions.md).
Every document approved by the owner in TrialAgents, or the user has explicitly chosen to export unapproved versions.
